assignment.review_focus: Close the verification gap analysis for PT9L. Specifically: (1) Determine whether any verification or validation record in the DHF corpus confirms that the object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance of ±0.2 °C applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans is intentional and justified against the design-input specification (which requires ±0.2 °C only for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C body-temperature range). (2) Determine whether any V&V record addresses Bluetooth-specific hazards or Bluetooth functional verification for PT9L, given that the Risk Management Report acknowledges Bluetooth transmission capability but no Bluetooth hazard verification evidence was found by the Risk Traceability Agent. (3) Determine whether the battery design-verification plan/report blood-pressure residue phrase (identified by Hardware Agent) appears in a pass/fail verdict section or only in a boilerplate/template section, and whether the overall battery verification record carries a signed pass verdict. (4) Identify whether any verification record explicitly references the PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 risk report (rather than V1.0) as the controlling risk document for verification closure. (5) Confirm whether the IEC 60601-1 test report referencing software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 (noted by Software Agent as absent from the evidence catalog) has any corresponding entry in the design output list or verification index.

input_package.goal: Check whether design inputs, verification plans, validation reports, external formal reports, and design confirmation evidence support each other.
input_package.system_prompt: Review verification and validation consistency using only supplied evidence IDs.

assignment.review_focus: Close the verification gap analysis for PT9L. Specifically: (1) Determine whether any verification or validation record in the DHF corpus confirms that the object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance of ±0.2 °C applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans is intentional and justified against the design-input specification (which requires ±0.2 °C only for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C body-temperature range). (2) Determine whether any V&V record addresses Bluetooth-specific hazards or Bluetooth functional verification for PT9L, given that the Risk Management Report acknowledges Bluetooth transmission capability but no Bluetooth hazard verification evidence was found by the Risk Traceability Agent. (3) Determine whether the battery design-verification plan/report blood-pressure residue phrase (identified by Hardware Agent) appears in a pass/fail verdict section or only in a boilerplate/template section, and whether the overall battery verification record carries a signed pass verdict. (4) Identify whether any verification record explicitly references the PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 risk report (rather than V1.0) as the controlling risk document for verification closure. agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

llm_output.summary: PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.
